Everything you need to ship from India to Venezuela or import from Venezuela to India: the trade agreement, routes and transit times, how your buyer imports, duties, regulators and documents.
India and Venezuela at a glance
No trade agreement with India. Venezuela is suspended from Mercosur.
India exports pharmaceuticals, food items, textiles and machinery. India has historically been a major buyer of Venezuelan crude, depending on sanctions licences.
Routes and transit times to Venezuela
35–50 days. Transhipment via Caribbean hubs (Cartagena, Kingston, Caucedo, Colón/Manzanillo) after crossing via the Mediterranean or the Cape.
Transit times are indicative port-to-port from Nhava Sheva / Mundra (sea) and Delhi / Mumbai (air). Routing changes (for example Red Sea diversions) can add 10–14 days.
Importing into Venezuela: what your buyer needs
The importer needs a RIF tax ID with SENIAT. A customs agent is required.
IMPORTANT: check US and other sanctions before any transaction. Payments, insurance and some counterparties may be restricted, and Indian banks are cautious.
Tariff mostly 0–35% depending on the product, plus 16% VAT (IVA).
Ministry of Health (MPPS) / INHRR: medicines, food registration

From Venezuela to India, and tips from the field
Crude oil when permitted under sanctions licences.
File the Bill of Entry through a licensed customs broker in India (YAM holds licence R-7/92).
Check the HS code in the Indian tariff, the DGFT import policy (free, restricted or prohibited) and any BIS, FSSAI, plant quarantine or other permit before the goods ship.
If an agreement applies, get the correct certificate of origin from the exporter to claim the lower duty.
Run sanctions screening on every party, vessel and bank before you commit.
